c-section: the delivery of a fetus by surgical incision through the abdominal wall and uterus (from the belief that Julius Caesar was born that way)
cs: a soft silver-white ductile metallic element (liquid at normal temperatures); the most electropositive and alkaline metal
cse: Canadian agency that gathers communications intelligence and assist law enforcement and security agencies
csis: Canada's main foreign intelligence agency that gathers and analyzes information to provide security intelligence for the Canadian government
cst: standard time in the 6th time zone west of Greenwich, reckoned at the 90th meridian; used in the central United States
